Pros and cons. I am really happy with how the app has changed in the year since I had it last. They have gamified it like Duolingo and that’s very motivating to complete different practice features and keep my streak going. However, I have a few complaints. 
1. What are the points for? Completing tasks earns points. Yay. But so what? There is nowhere on that app that shows how much we have earned. And there isn’t anything to DO with them, so who cares? Nice try, but falls flat in the follow-through.
2. The Daily Practice feature is glitchy. Half the time, I have to complete a song twice because doing it one time isn’t enough to get the golden check mark and get credit as “completed.” 
3. The Daily Practice and Daily Quests have NOTHING to do with each other. I don’t understand why there are TWO different ways we have to tick all the boxes. Pick one or the other. And you can’t just do the DQs and ignore the DPs because to get points in the skills category you have to do the DPs. 
And 4. The songs they make me practice in the Daily Practice are COMPLETELY beyond my current skill level springing really fast paced and complicated strum patterns on me that I haven’t even learned yet. The app should be smart enough NOT to dump hard stuff on someone early in the Learning Path. 
The app has a lot of potential, but it feels like it is being run/created by 3 different bosses who have small egos and refused to communicate with each other.

Good Option: Needs Tuning. I’m a brand new uke owner so you can take my review with a grain of salt. I haven’t played an instrument in over 20 years, so attempting a self taught approach will be interesting. I was pleased to find this app and decided to try it mainly for the tuner capabilities and price point, but I was drawn in by the lessons it offered. 

I had found another app that also had a learn to play function, but the cost was nearly triple fire the other one. I decided to give it the week trial, but cancelled before the trial was over for a few reasons. 

Pros: The app is fairly easy to navigate. It offers a nice selection of songs to play along with in a variety of skill levels. The instructor I have had so far in the videos is friendly and nice to listen to. I like that he provides options for sons of the chords if you Made be Sterling with goes to position your hand in the neck/frets. The tuner appears to be accurate and the chord tracking capabilities is nice as it gives you feedback for your performance. 

Cons: It’s kind of buggy. I have used the app at least one a day during the trial and each day I experienced some kind of glitch. On the lesson path and the practice options, I have experienced multiple times of the app not acknowledging that I have played along with the song/lesson. This caused me to have to repeat the video multiple times before it gave me the “continue” button. The chord tracking feature is nice as it gives you feedback on if you have hit the desired note, however, there have been many times I hear no audio in my headset when this feature is being used. The audio has also cut in and out during the lesson. This is the only app I have any issues with my AirPods connecting to my phone. Sometimes I can just back out and go back in, but other times I have had to close and restart it. The other big issue is that I had randomly shut off on me. Obviously it’s not a battery issue since it is an app and my phone still has plenty of power. 

I really wanted to like this app, but I can’t justify spending the full price on it for it to work when it decides it wants to.

Sometimes it’s hard to see which fingers go where in the videos. A close up or still frame or something would help for more complicated cords.

I love being able to slow songs down for learning.

Lastly I look forward to more lessons and songs!
